author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jacob Young dealing with hand soreness
desc: Washington Nationals manager Blake Butera said Jacob Young was unavailable for Sunday's 5-3 loss to the New York Yankees due to a sore left hand.
impact: Young has missed the Nationals' last two games while dealing with lingering soreness. Butera said the outfielder will likely need 4-5 days for his hand to regain full strength, making him a candidate to return when the Nationals resume play on Friday against the Athletics following the All-Star break.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Sam Antonacci goes deep in win over Athletics
desc: Sam Antonacci went 1-for-4 in Sunday's 9-1 win over the Athletics with a solo home run.
impact: Antonacci continues a steady stretch at the plate of late, collecting hits in 11 of his last 15 contests. The outfielder has rewarded manager Will Venable with an impactful option as part of a streaky White Sox lineup, slashing .287 with six home runs, 27 RBI, 48 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases across 75 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Braden Montgomery drives in four in win over Athletics
desc: Braden Montgomery went 2-for-4 in a win over the Athletics with a home run, one run scored, and four RBI.
impact: Montgomery continues a steady stretch of late, reaching base in eight of his last 10 contests. The 23-year-old has struggled with inconsistent stretches at the plate for manager Will Venable, hitting .231 with three home runs, 12 RBI, and 15 runs scored through 29 games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jonathan Aranda blasts one over fence Sunday
desc: Jonathan Aranda went 1-for-3 with a home run, one run scored and two RBI in Sunday's 8-2 loss to the Seattle Mariners.
impact: Aranda hit a two-run, opposite-field homer in the eighth inning, accounting for the Tampa Bay Rays' only runs of the game. He heads into the All-Star break on a high note, riding a five-game hitting streak while slashing .297/.394/.471 with an .865 OPS and 14 home runs on the season.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Noah Schultz cruises through five in win over Athletics
desc: Noah Schultz allowed one earned run on four hits while striking out four over five innings in Sunday's win over the Athletics.
impact: Schultz is in the middle of a dismal stretch on the mound, allowing three earned runs or more in six of his last seven trips to the mound. The left-hander remains one of the more disappointing arms in the White Sox rotation for manager Will Venable, posting a 5.60 ERA and 1.36 WHIP with a 3-6 record and 1.6 K/BB ratio through 11 starts.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Ian Seymour struggles in short outing Sunday
desc: Ian Seymour allowed five earned runs on six hits and three walks while striking out three across 3.1 innings in Sunday's 8-2 loss to the Seattle Mariners.
impact: While Seymour opened with a scoreless first inning, he allowed three runs in the second and was unable to escape the fourth after surrendering a two-run homer and a single. He heads into the All-Star break with a 4.59 ERA and 1.16 WHIP across 33 appearances, including six starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: J.T. Ginn torched early in loss to White Sox
desc: J.T. Ginn allowed eight earned runs on six hits and three walks while striking out seven through 4 1/3 innings in Sunday's loss to the White Sox.
impact: Ginn has offered mixed results on the mound of late, allowing three earned runs or more in four of his last eight trips to the mound. The right-hander remains one of the more reliable arms in an underwhelming Athletics rotation for manager Mark Kotsay, posting a 3.67 ERA and 1.25 WHIP with a 7-6 record and 8.1 K/9 ratio through 21 appearances.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong swipes bag Sunday
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong went 1-for-3 with two walks, two runs scored, one RBI and a stolen base in Sunday's 8-4 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
impact: Crow-Armstrong continues to deliver for fantasy managers, reaching base safely in nine of his first 10 games in July while adding three home runs and four stolen bases. He heads into the All-Star break slashing .291/.386/.531 with 21 homers and 24 stolen bases.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Logan Webb will not pitch in All-Star game
desc: The Giants say Logan Webb will not pitch in Tuesday's All-Star game.
impact: Webb is healthy heading into the break. He will pitch next weekend against the Mariners.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Alex Bregman goes deep Sunday
desc: Alex Bregman went 3-for-5 with a home run, a double, two runs scored and four RBI in Sunday's 8-4 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
impact: Bregman closed out the first half of the season on a high note, recording his first three-hit game since April 22 while collecting two extra-base hits, including a three-run homer in the seventh inning. He enters the All-Star break slashing .241/.336/.359 with nine home runs.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Shea Langeliers goes deep in loss to White Sox
desc: Shea Langeliers went 1-for-4 in Sunday's 9-1 loss to the Athletics with a solo home run.
impact: Langeliers has provided mixed results at the plate of late, collecting hits in four of his last eight contests. The catcher continues to reward manager Mark Kotsay with one of the few impactful bats in an inconsistent Athletics lineup, carrying an .807 OPS with 21 home runs, 46 RBI, 52 runs scored, and two stolen bases across 86 games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Matthew Boyd picks up win Sunday
desc: Matthew Boyd allowed four runs on six hits, one walk and two hit batters while striking out three across 6.1 innings in Sunday's 8-4 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
impact: Although Boyd allowed his most runs since returning from the injured list on June 25, he still earned his third straight victory. Since rejoining the rotation, he has surrendered seven earned runs across 22 innings. He closes the first half of the season with a 4.50 ERA and 1.28 WHIP.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Jose Soriano grinds through five in loss to Twins
desc: Jose Soriano allowed three earned runs on five hits and two walks over five innings in Sunday's loss to the Twins.
impact: Soriano has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in five of his last seven trips to the mound. The right-hander remains one of the more reliable starting options as part of an underperforming Angels rotation for manager Kurt Suzuki, carrying a 3.49 ERA and 1.29 WHIP with an 8-6 record and 9.3 K/9 ratio across 20 starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Josh Lowe goes deep in loss to Twins
desc: Josh Lowe went 1-for-4 in Sunday's 4-2 loss to the Twins with a solo home run.
impact: Lowe continues a solid stretch since returning from injury, getting on base in 12 of his last 15 contests. The outfielder continues to work back from a dismal start to the season for manager Kurt Suzuki, hitting .208 with eight home runs, 21 RBI, 17 runs scored, and three stolen bases through 60 games.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Griffin Conine hits homer Sunday
desc: Griffin Conine went 1-for-2 with a solo home run in Sunday's 5-2 loss to the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: Conine pinch-hit for Rece Hinds in the seventh inning and struck out swinging. However, he remained in the game and responded with a 442-foot home run off Cade Smith in the ninth inning. Across 30 at-bats in July, he is slashing .233/.343/.467.
